hook: A trampoline jumper, a bungee cord and a car's suspension all trade energy back and forth between motion and a stretched or squeezed spring. Follow the energy and you can find the top speed of an oscillator without knowing anything about its timing.

prereq.q: A spring with k = 400 N/m is compressed 0.050 m. How much elastic potential energy does it store?
When is the mechanical energy of a system constant?
options: When no nonconservative forces (like friction) do work on it
When the object moves at constant speed
When the net force is zero
prereq.why: Mechanical energy changes only when nonconservative or external forces do work.

prereq.q: In SHM, where is the object's speed greatest?
prereq.why: The restoring force has sped it up all the way to x = 0.

figure.caption: Energy against position for a block on a spring, with bar charts at three positions.

chain.cause: The block is released from rest at x = A
chain.effect: all the system's energy is spring potential energy, ½kA²

chain.cause: The spring pushes the block toward x = 0 and does positive work on it
chain.effect: spring energy turns into kinetic energy

chain.cause: At x = 0 the spring is relaxed
chain.effect: all the energy is kinetic and the block moves at top speed

chain.cause: No friction removes energy from the system
chain.effect: the total stays ½kA², so the block reaches the same distance A on the other side

ideas: For a block and spring with no friction, E = K + Us is constant. Name the system (block + spring) and the condition (no friction) before you use it.
The total energy is set by the amplitude: E = ½kA². At the turning points K = 0; at equilibrium Us = 0 and K = E.
U<sub>s</sub> = ½kx² goes as x², so at x = A/2 the spring holds only a quarter of the energy. Energy graphs against position are parabolas, and the total is a flat line.
For a pendulum, the energy trades between kinetic and gravitational potential energy: mgΔy = ½mv² at the bottom.

misconception.wrong: Halfway to the turning point the energy is half kinetic and half potential.
misconception.right: Potential energy goes as x², so at x = A/2 the spring holds ¼ of the energy and the block has ¾ as kinetic energy. The half-and-half point is at x = A/√2.

summary: With no friction the mechanical energy of an oscillator is constant: for a block on a spring E = ½kA², all potential at the turning points and all kinetic at equilibrium; doubling the amplitude quadruples the energy.
